text:
viv: kicking off a short thread on the 'variant-oracle' idea: single service that emits compact traffic decisions and fallback directives for canaries/A-Bs/experiments. want to align on API shape + operational safety.

noah: variant-oracle sounds good. quick ask: what invariants do we enforce automatically vs what remains manual?

viv: minimal set: 1) never increase traffic for a variant that fails correctness checks, 2) never exceed tenant budget caps, 3) backoff on noisy signals to avoid flip-flop. everything else tunable per-policy.

rachel: signals matrix? we need to be explicit. my list: correctness tests (golden set), online quality deltas (embed similarity / hallucination heuristics), infrastructure signals (p99 latency, queue depth), cost burn, probe success.

diego: add cold-start probes: runtime should report warmup state. oracle shouldn't route more weight until warm_ack true (or planned_warm_volume communicated).

note: ops-bot: rollout started variant=oracle-v1 weight=0.5% id=orcl-20260321-09

viv: API sketch: Decide(tenant_id, region, context_tags, local_metrics_summary) -> [Decision{variant, weight_pct, decision_id, expires_at, safety_level, reason_codes}]. decisions are advisory; runtime must ack acceptance with Ack(decision_id, applied_weight, warm_ack).

noah: safety_level enum idea: STRONG, CAUTIOUS, OBSERVATIONAL. STRONG implies immediate revert on correctness flags; CAUTIOUS allows staged ramp with auto-shrink.

rachel: telemetry contract: every decision_id must be stamped on subsequent requests/metrics. also record pre/post windows for causal analysis.

diego: orchestration detail: local proxy caches last Decision and can act offline for short windows. but we need monotonic generation numbers to avoid applying stale decisions after reconnect. Decision should carry generation and nonce.

viv: on fallback semantics: two axes: immediacy (immediate vs staged) and severity (revert all vs reduce by X%). default mapping: correctness failure -> immediate full revert; perf/cost degradation -> staged reduce by step% and hold for cool_down period.

noah: propose a per-tenant daily rollback budget to prevent runaway rollbacks from noisy metrics. also a per-tenant min_interval between escalations (default 3m).

rachel: smoothing windows: system uses short window (30s) for fast detection, and medium window (5m) for confirmation. decisions require weighted evidence across windows.

diego: autoscaler interplay: oracle should emit planned_traffic_curve to autoscaler: {t+0m: 1%, t+5m:6%, t+10m:11%}. scaler can accept and provision. otherwise we risk reactive scaling that triggers perf signals.

viv: experiments integration: oracle should support experiment contexts (opt-in cohorts) and provide stable assignment keys so variant stickiness remains consistent for users across retries.

ops-bot: alert: orcl-20260321-09 p99 +14% at 1806001402 tagging thread

rachel: seen. in policy model we need to classify alerts into signal buckets: correctness vs performance vs flakiness. flakiness -> ignore until repeated, performance -> staged adjust, correctness -> revert.

noah: on implementation: make the Decision protobuf tiny. fields: tenant, region, generation, decision_id, actions[{variant, delta_pct, hard_revert_bool}], expiry_ts, reason_tags[], planned_traffic_curve_url(optional). keep extension points for policy metadata.

diego: runtime shim changes: 1) accept decisions, 2) provide warm_ack RPC, 3) submit local metric summaries and probe results at interval. keep RPCs lightweight.

viv: ops expectations: 1) roll-forward path when oracle is healthy, 2) manual override hook to freeze a tenant to a specific policy, 3) audit trail and one-click revert in console.

rachel: migration plan: backwards compatible flag: runtime reads oracle if flag set, else uses legacy canary. start with internal tenants, then opt-in beta customers.

noah: locks and leader election: oracle will be multi-region; decisions should be computed per-tenant in a single logical leader to avoid splits. use consistent hashing to pick leader region for tenant.

diego: dispute resolution: if local proxies disagree with oracle (e.g., metrics mismatch), proxies can request a rapid re-eval RPC. include a 'hold' token to prevent immediate changes until re-eval completes.

viv: security note: decision channel must be signed/authorized. cannot let a rogue controller alter traffic. add per-tenant signing keys and nonce checks.

ops-bot: note: compliance ask from legal: store decision audit for 365 days. tagging this thread.

viv: ok owners: rachel -> signals and telemetry contract, diego -> runtime shim + autoscaler contract, noah -> leader election and ops safety, i'll own decision proto + policy reference implementation. timeline: proto PR by Thu, RFC draft by next Tue.

rachel: i'll include a sample YAML policy matrix with strong/soft mappings and an example of the planned_traffic_curve.

noah: small perf nit: do not call Decide synchronously on every request. proxies should poll or subscribe to updates; only send summaries periodically.

diego: agreed. streaming watch channel with compact diffs is most efficient.

viv: thanks all. i'll open a stub RFC and assign reviewers. meeting to follow at 11am PT tomorrow to walk through shapes.

ops-bot: reminder: follow-up checklist created: https://go/redwood/rfc-oracle-checklist

viv: great. closing this thread.
